fields.default:
You need to link a Contact to a Supplier in ERPNext. Here's exactly how:

Step-by-Step: Link a User to the Supplier Portal
Step 1 — Make sure the user exists
Go to Settings → User and confirm the person has an ERPNext login account. Note their exact email address (e.g. john@acme.com).

Step 2 — Open or create their Contact record
Go to CRM → Contact (or search "Contact" in the search bar).
Either find an existing contact for this person, or click New.
Fill in:

First Name / Last Name
Email ID — must be the exact same email as their ERPNext login


Step 3 — Add the Dynamic Link (the critical step)
Still on the Contact form, scroll down to the Links table (sometimes labeled "Links" or "Reference Doctype").
Click Add Row:
FieldValueLink TypeSupplierLink NameSelect the supplier record (e.g. Acme Supplies Ltd)
Save the Contact.

Step 4 — Assign the portal role
Go back to Settings → User, open that user's account, and in the Roles table add:

Supplier Portal User

Save.

Step 5 — Test
Log in as that user and visit /supplier-portal. The portal will now resolve:
john@acme.com → Contact → Dynamic Link → Acme Supplies Ltd ✓

Quick way to verify the link is set correctly
Run this in ERPNext → Settings → System Console (Python tab):
pythonuser = "john@acme.com"  # change this

contact = frappe.db.get_value("Contact", {"email_id": user})
print("Contact:", contact)

if contact:
    link = frappe.db.get_value("Dynamic Link", {
        "parenttype": "Contact",
        "parent": contact,
        "link_doctype": "Supplier"
    }, "link_name")
    print("Supplier:", link)
else:
    print("No contact found for this email")
If it prints a Supplier name, the portal will work. If it prints None, the Dynamic Link row is missing.

Same process for Customer Portal
Identical steps — just use Link Type = Customer instead of Supplier, and assign the Customer Portal User role.
